post.description:
Cancel for the club, the way the club's own cancel does.

- `at_period_end: true`: the club keeps what it paid for (or its trial)
  until `current_period_end`, then Free. Razorpay stops at the end of the
  cycle for an active subscription, at once for any other.
- `at_period_end: false`: Razorpay stops now and so does access: the club
  goes to Free, or back to an admin's grant it had before a checkout.
- A checkout still pending is closed and the club goes back to what it had.
- A plan an admin granted has nothing at Razorpay; it is cancelled here.
- A complimentary plan is revoked now, whatever `at_period_end` says:
  the club goes to Free.

409 NOTHING_TO_CANCEL when it is cancelled already (and, for `false`, no
paid-for days are left to end). 502 RAZORPAY_ERROR when Razorpay refuses:
nothing is changed here then, so the club is never shown cancelled while
Razorpay can still charge it.

plan until the new end; nothing is charged or cancelled.

Refused (422 NOT_PAST_DUE) for any other status, and (422 NEVER_PAID) for
a Razorpay subscription that was never paid for -- it has no access to
keep; move the club to a plan instead.

post.description:
A fresh set of eight, shown once, for a current authenticator code;
every earlier one stops working. Also how codes issued before the
current format are replaced. Never for an admin acting as the account
(403 NOT_WHILE_IMPERSONATING): the codes get past its second factor.

post.description:
Generates a secret and returns the otpauth:// URI to scan.

Two steps on purpose: the secret is stored but not enabled until the user
proves they can read a code from it. Enabling here would lock out anyone
whose authenticator failed to scan. Stored encrypted when the server has
a key (app.api.auth.totp).
post.summary: Start two-factor enrolment

post.description:
Mint a short-lived hand-off token for another account.

This is the most dangerous capability in the product, so it is fenced:

- admins only, and never targeting another admin -- an admin who could
  impersonate a peer could act as them and leave the log pointing at the
  wrong person
- the token lives for two minutes and is exchanged for a session
  immediately
- the resulting session carries `impersonated_by`, so it stays
  identifiable for its whole life rather than only at creation
- the attempt is recorded before the token is returned, so a token that
  is minted and never used is still in the log
- it needs a reason, at least IMPERSONATION_REASON_MIN characters, kept
  with the attempt in the log: a session nobody can explain later is
  one nobody can review (422 REASON_REQUIRED without one)

It was deliberately not built until the audit log existed, because an
admin acting as a user with no record of it is precisely the thing worth
refusing.

booked as a guest under the address is brought into the account. A wrong

one kills the code (CODE_LOCKED); an old, replaced or absent one is

Sign in with Google

post.description:
The dashboards' "Continue with Google". The ID token is checked as
`/auth/google` checks the web's (audience APP_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID,
signature, issuer, expiry; Google must have verified the address), and
its address signs in an account that already exists. None is ever made.

- `scope: "club"`: an active club team member with the address (a session
  on the club's account, with `member_id`), else the club's own login
  account. 403 CLUB_UNAVAILABLE / CLUB_NOT_VERIFIED as on `/auth/token`.
- `scope: "admin"`: an admin account only.

Anything else -- no account, an app user, a guest, the other dashboard's
account -- is the same 401 GOOGLE_NO_ACCOUNT. Then as `/auth/token`: 403
ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED; 401 TOTP_REQUIRED when the account has two-factor
(send the same id_token again with `totp_code`) and TOTP_INVALID; 429
LOGIN_LOCKED; the same answer, session and cookies. 401
INVALID_GOOGLE_TOKEN for a token Google would not vouch for; 503
GOOGLE_UNAVAILABLE when its certificates can't be fetched.
post.summary: Sign in to the club dashboard or the main portal with Google

post.description:
Turn the hand-off token into a session as the target account.

Unauthenticated by design -- the token is the credential. It is accepted
only if it is of type `impersonation`, still carries the admin that
minted it, and has not been exchanged before (its `jti` becomes the
session's id: a second exchange finds it taken). The admin must still be
an active admin allowed to impersonate.

The session has a row like any other -- the target sees it on their
Security page and can end it -- carries `impersonated_by`, ends
IMPERSONATION_SESSION_MINUTES (30 to 60) after this, and is never
renewed: there is no refresh token (`refresh_token` is empty, and the
refresh cookie is cleared). The exchange is in the audit log.
post.summary: Exchange a hand-off token for a session

post.description:
Ends the session on the server, then clears the httpOnly auth cookies
set by /auth/token and /auth/refresh (client-side JS can't clear those
itself).

The session is named by the refresh token -- the `token` form field, as
/auth/refresh takes it, or the `refresh_token` cookie -- and by a live
access token when one is sent too. The refresh token is what matters: it
outlives the access token, so a sign-out after the access token expired
(a dashboard tab left open, a phone back from the background) still ends
the session, and a copied cookie stops working at once instead of when
it would have expired. Always 200, whatever was or wasn't sent.
post.summary: Sign out: end this session and clear the auth cookies

get.summary: get current user info

post.description:
Always 200 `{"sent": true}`, at once, whatever the address: it never says
whether there is an account. After the response, when the address has an
app account that signs in with a password, a six-digit code goes to it
(good for fifteen minutes; at most one a minute and ten a day per
address, past which nothing goes). Google and Apple accounts get nothing.
post.summary: Send a code to reset a forgotten password

post.description:
The code and the new password: on a match the password is set, every
other session ends, the address counts as verified, whatever was booked
as a guest under it comes into the account, and the answer is the same
tokens as `/auth/token` (the person is signed in).

A wrong code -- or an address with no live code, account or not -- is a
400 CODE_INVALID with `errors.attempts_left`; the fifth wrong try kills
the code (CODE_LOCKED); an old, used or replaced one is CODE_EXPIRED. An
account with two-factor on also needs `totp_code`: 401 TOTP_REQUIRED
without it, TOTP_INVALID (a wrong try) when it is wrong.
post.summary: Set a new password with the code from the email, and sign in

post.description:
A new access token -- and a NEW refresh token, which replaces the one
sent: keep the one in the answer (the body, and the `refresh_token`
cookie). It expires when the one sent would have.

The one sent stays good until the new one is first used: presented
again before that (the answer was lost, the app was killed mid-refresh,
two tabs refreshed together) it is answered with the same new refresh
token again, however much later. Once the new one has been used, the
old one -- or anything older -- ends the session (401 SESSION_REUSED):
two parties holding one session means one of them stole it.
post.summary: refresh access token

post.description:
Stop the club's Razorpay subscription. The club keeps its plan until
`current_period_end` -- the end of what it paid for, or of its trial --
and then falls to Free.

A paid subscription is cancelled at Razorpay at the end of its cycle; a
trial, a past-due or a paused one at once (nothing more is owed on it).
A checkout still pending is cancelled at once and the club goes back to
what it had. Asking twice changes nothing. A plan an admin granted by
hand has nothing at Razorpay to cancel (409 NO_SUBSCRIPTION).

post.description:
Open a Razorpay checkout for a public plan, by `plan_id` or `plan_key`.

Nothing is granted here. The subscription is recorded `pending` and the
club keeps what it had until Razorpay confirms: `authenticated` starts a
trial (when the plan has one and the club never had a trial), `activated`
/ `charged` make it active. An unpaid checkout falls back after a day,
which is also when the Razorpay link stops working.

Refused: a club on a complimentary plan (409 COMPLIMENTARY_PLAN: its plan
is changed by talking to us; once the comp has ended, checkout works as
usual), a plan not on the pricing page (404 PLAN_NOT_AVAILABLE), one
priced on request (422 CONTACT_SALES), a free one (422 FREE_PLAN), and a
second checkout while a Razorpay subscription can still charge the club
(409 SUBSCRIPTION_EXISTS). A pending checkout the club never authorised is
the exception: it is cancelled at Razorpay and replaced.

get.description:
The ticket as a PNG, for showing on screen.

The app drew its own ticket -- a hardcoded card with its own colours and
its own QR -- and the event website drew a third one. Only the PDF
download carried the club's design. This is the same template, the same
payload and the same engine as the PDF, so what the attendee sees in the
app is the ticket the club designed.

Same access rule as the PDF: the ticket's owner, the owning club, or an
admin. A QR is an entry pass, not a public image.

Tagged like the PDF, from the same fingerprint (_document_etag, with
"-png"): a 304 without drawing when If-None-Match names it. The
fingerprint names the revocation too, so a revoked ticket can never be
answered 304 against the picture a phone kept while it still worked.

A revoked ticket is refused (410, TICKET_REVOKED): the door will not
open on this QR, so nothing here draws one.
get.summary: Get ticket as an image

get.description:
Generate and download a PDF for the ticket.

Its ETag names this ticket as drawn (_document_etag). Asked again with
that tag in If-None-Match, an unchanged ticket is a 304, decided without
drawing it or reading the bucket. The access check comes first.

A revoked ticket is refused (410, TICKET_REVOKED), as the emailed link's
own download has always been (app/api/emails/router.py). Revoking it also
changes the fingerprint, so the copy kept in the bucket is retired and no
held ETag matches.
get.summary: Get ticket PDF

get.description:
Generate and download an Apple Wallet pass (.pkpass) for the ticket.

Requires authentication. The pass can be added to Apple Wallet on iOS devices.

A revoked ticket is refused (410, TICKET_REVOKED). A pass already in
Wallet is not recalled by this -- there is no push service registered for
these passes -- but it stops being handed out, and the door refuses the
barcode on it (app/api/checkins).

post.description:
The raw MIME, for one envelope recipient, signed by the Worker
(club_mailbox/cloudflare.py: the signature is checked from the headers
before the body is read). Kept for the club the address is (or for the
team's desk: support@ / sales@; or the platform's own inbox: admin@,
info@, ...), and the Worker told what to do.

Answers: 200 `{"action": "accept"}` (kept, or kept before); 200
`{"action": "reject", "reason", "text"}` -- the Worker rejects the mail
in the SMTP session with `text` (no such address, a closed mailbox,
too large); 401 unsigned, stale or another key's (or, with
APP_MAILBOX_HOOK_REQUIRE_BODY_SIGNATURE on, signed only the older way);
400 a body that isn't the signed size (or, v2, the signed body); 503 the hook isn't set up (APP_MAILBOX_HOOK_SECRET) or
the mail couldn't be kept now: the Worker gives the sender a temporary
error, and the mail comes again. Never a mail, an address or the body in
the log.

get.description:
Stream every row matching the filters, not just the page on screen.

Behind `export_data` rather than plain AdminAuth: a viewer can already
page the list, but handing out the whole user base as one file is a
different act from reading a screen of it, and it is the one the audit
log and the role split care about.

Streamed in chunks rather than assembled and returned: the box this runs
on has a few hundred megabytes of headroom, and a full export held in
memory as Python objects is the kind of thing that takes the API down
with it. Each chunk starts where the last one ended (a keyset on the
sort column and id), so chunk n costs what chunk 1 did; it skipped past
every earlier row by OFFSET, which made a large export quadratic.

`format=xlsx`: the same rows as an Excel workbook, written a chunk at a
time to a temporary file on a worker thread, then sent from disk.

The request's own session is used while streaming, which is safe here:
FastAPI closes the dependency exit stack after the response body has
been sent, so a `yield` dependency outlives the generator that produced
the body. `test_export_pages_past_one_chunk` is what actually holds that
down -- it reads several chunks, so a session closed early fails it.
